<reason>Side A won the sequencing clash: existing counselling and portals are not being switched off, so the next discretionary pound should protect hard-to-rebuild recurring community before expanding duplicative platforms. A also damaged B's scale claim by distinguishing impressions from repeated support, and pressed the anonymity-versus-monitoring tension. B's inclusion case for disabled, working, and remote students remained powerful, but B never fully answered the existing-services baseline or irreversibility, and its clipped first rebuttal weakened delivery.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's Rebuttal 1 was decisive: reframing digital as a coordinator that needs real clubs and spaces to coordinate, while recasting 500 contacts versus 50 recurring participants as contact versus care.</best_rebuttal>
